name: Ma Huateng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Ma Huateng, also known as Pony Ma, is the chairman and CEO of Chinese internet giant Tencent Holdings.
Tencent's popular social messaging app WeChat has over 1.4 billion monthly users.
Known at home for mobile games such as battle game Honor of Kings, Tencent is also one of the largest videogame publishers globally and has acquired a stake in U.S. videogame company Epic Games.
It has also invested in electric car maker Tesla and music-streaming service Spotify, which in turn has a stake in its Tencent Music.

Ma has been ramping up investments in AI to make the company's Hunyuan family of models stand out amid fierce competition at home. He hired in 2026 former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu to lead Tencent's AI efforts.
forbes_facts: Ma led research and development of internet paging system at China Motion Telecom Development before starting Tencent in 1998.

name: Stephen Ross
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate and sports magnate Stephen Ross was a tax attorney before founding Related Companies in 1972 as an affordable housing developer.
In all, Related has developed or acquired more than $60 billion worth of properties of all kinds from California to Abu Dhabi to London.
After a decade of planning and construction, Related Co.'s Hudson Yards on Manhattan's west side opened to the public in March 2019.
In July 2024, Ross formed a new real estate firm, Related Ross, in West Palm Beach, Florida.
Ross also owns a stake in the Miami Dolphins NFL team and the Formula One Miami Grand Prix, plus stakes in Equinox Fitness and SoulCycle.
In December 2024, he sold a 13% stake in the Dolphins, the Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open to Ares Management and the owners of the NBA's Brooklyn Nets at an $8.1 billion valuation.
forbes_facts: The single largest donor to alma mater University of Michigan, Ross has given a total of $480 million, including $100 million announced in February 2020.
Ross' uncle, oil tycoon Max Fisher, was on The Forbes 400 for 23 years until his death in 2005.

name: Ann Walton Kroenke
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Ann Walton Kroenke is one of two daughters of Bud Walton, who helped his brother, Sam, build Walmart into a retail giant.
She inherited part of Bud's stake in the retailer when he died in 1995.
A registered nurse, Walton Kroenke is not involved with Walmart as a board member or an executive.
Her husband is billionaire real estate and sports mogul Stan Kroenke.
He owns the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche, Colorado Rapids and Arsenal Football Club in the U.K.

name: Riley Bechtel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Riley Bechtel ran Bechtel, his family's construction and engineering firm, from 1990 to 2014.
He stepped down as CEO in 2014 after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.
His son Brendan is the current chairman and CEO and the fifth generation to run the company.
Together, Riley, his siblings and their children hold an estimated 40% stake in Bechtel.
Bechtel is the company behind projects such as the Hoover Dam and San Francisco's Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) system.
forbes_facts: Riley Bechtel joined Bechtel in 1981 as a contract coordinator.

name: Mitchell Morgan
forbes_bio: Mitchell Morgan is the founder, CEO and owner of Conshohocken, Pennsylvania-based Morgan Properties, the third-largest owner of apartments in the U.S.
Morgan Properties owns more than 350 properties with over 97,000 units in 20 states.
Morgan founded the company in the Philadelphia suburb of King of Prussia in 1985 with a partner and took sole ownership in 1996.
Morgan Properties' first major deal was the 2007 acquisition of a 17,000-unit portfolio from the Kushner Companies for $1.9 billion alongside AIG.
Before entering the real estate business, Morgan worked as an accountant while taking night classes to earn a law degree at Temple University.
forbes_facts: Morgan owns a stake in the NFL's Washington Commanders and in Major League Baseball's Philadelphia Phillies
Morgan's first job was working as a shoe salesman at his father's shoe store in Philadelphia to pay his way through college at Temple.

name: Rupert Johnson Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Rupert Johnson Jr. is the vice chairman of Franklin Resources, a global investment management firm also called Franklin Templeton Investments.
He is the largest shareholder in the firm with 20%. His half brother Charles, who chaired the company until 2013, is a close second.
Their father, Rupert Sr., founded Franklin Distributors in 1947; the business grew and went public in 1983.
Rupert Jr. joined in 1965 and has been vice chairman since 1999. His nephew Gregory Johnson now serves as chairman.
forbes_facts: His father Rupert named the company after Benjamin Franklin who he believed epitomized the ideas of frugality and prudence in regard to saving and investing.
Rupert pledged $100 million to his alma mater, Washington and Lee University, in 2007, $85 million of which has been designated for scholarships.

name: Willy Michel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Willy Michel is the cofounder of Ypsomed Selfcare Solutions, a Swiss pharma company that develops self-injection and diagnostic systems.
Ypsomed was started in 2003 out of Disetronic Holding, which Michel founded in 1984 with his brother and sold to Roche for $1.2 billion.
As part of the sale agreement, Michel got the injection business back from Roche for $310 million, forming what is known as Ypsomed today.
Michel and his three children together own a 71% stake in the company.
In 2025, Michel bought Ypsomed's diabetes business for over $500 million; it's now a part of TecMed, another medical company he founded.
forbes_facts: Michel founded an art museum with his collection of Franz Gertsch portraits.
Michel reportedly owns a yacht called the Vive La Vie that features rotating beds, a disco dance floor and floating glass staircase.

name: Margarita Louis-Dreyfus
name_chinese: 玛格丽塔·路易斯·德莱弗斯
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Margarita Louis-Dreyfus is the majority owner and chairwoman of agricultural commodities giant Louis-Dreyfus.
Her husband Robert Louis-Dreyfus died of leukemia in 2009, leaving her a 69.6% stake in the now 167-year-old business.
She reportedly pledged her shares to take out a $1 billion loan in 2019 to buy out minority stakes owned by family members.
In 2016, she sold French soccer team Olympique Marseille to former Dodgers owner Frank McCourt, but held onto a 5% stake.
That same year, she gave birth to twins at age 53. Her reported partner is Philipp Hildebrand, vice chairman of BlackRock.
forbes_facts: Born and raised in Russia, Louis-Dreyfus was reportedly orphaned at age 11 when her parents died in a train crash.
Before meeting Robert on a flight in 1988, she sold computer parts.

name: Gilles Martin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Gilles Martin is the executive chairman of Eurofins Scientific, a Luxembourg-based laboratory services company listed on the French stock exchange.
Martin, who founded the original lab in 1987, owns an estimated 22% of the company through the family's holding company Analytical Bioventures.
His brother Yves-Loic owns an estimated 10% stake. He served as CTO from 1998 until 2015 and now is a board member.
Eurofins has 900 labs in 61 countries and is prominent in food and pharmaceutical products testing.
